payload.body: examiner, round 1: writing the exam at fleet/tests/exams/run_184/test_factory_roles.mjs (EXAM PATHS maps it off fleet/tests/test_factory_roles.mjs, so ROOT is four levels up, not two). Plan: pure static read of the three role files — no import of any sibling module, no fixture, no spawn. Leg (a) reads each path with fs, asserts non-empty and sums per-file whitespace word counts (per-file sum, not the cat-concat count, is what the leg's words say and is the conservative measure). Leg (b) encodes the five prompt-section literals as exact-occurrence-count-1 checks and the rest as sentence-scoped regex pairs, where a sentence is a maximal run bounded by . ! ? or newline. Leg (c) is whole-word, case-insensitive for the four grading words and case-sensitive for the three shouted imperatives, over all three files. Leg (d) is line-scoped over implement.md and exam.md only. Existence is asserted before any read so the red at BASE reads as the absent role files, not ENOENT.

payload.author: impl:4@run-184
payload.body: Approach: three role files under factory/roles/, seeded from the prototype's IMPL_SYS/EXAM_SYS register (factory/proto/loop.mjs:118-119) and fleet/roles/resolver.md's three rules. Budget ~350/200/300 words to stay under the 900 sum. Writing the critical sentences (FILES/only-listed, TEST COMMAND/until, note/export, only-exam, not-create) each on one physical line and as one sentence, so a peer exam that splits on either lines or periods reads them the same way. No grading vocabulary (blocking/minor/severity/verdict), no shouted imperatives, and a single 'Do not run git' line per producer file. I write no exam file — fleet/tests/test_factory_roles.mjs is the peer's.

payload.body: Task 1 approach: factory/worker.mjs as one query() per dispatch. startWorker(opts, deps) builds the options object (settingSources: [], permissionMode bypassPermissions, cwd/systemPrompt/model, disallowedTools with Bash(git *)/WebFetch/WebSearch/Agent, outputFormat only when schema, mcpServers passed through) with an in-process PreToolUse hook closing over the call's own denials array, calls deps.query() synchronously and answers { promise, handle } where handle IS the Query object query() returns; runWorker is startWorker(...).promise; interruptWorker(handle) awaits handle.interrupt() once. The SDK import is a top-level dynamic import in a try/catch so the module still loads in a tree with no fleet/node_modules — the exam drives a fake deps.query and must never need the real package on disk.
